options.plan: Upstream release 26.8.0; commercial support not assessed
options.region: Operator-selected hosting; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: One customer realm; confidential browser OIDC/SAML; local-user SCIM; no broker, Organizations or outbound bridge

conditions: Register an OIDC client and enable Standard Flow for authorization-code login.
Configure exact redirect URIs, client authentication and the intended PKCE policy; documentation support does not verify a deployment.
This assertion concerns downstream application clients, not upstream enterprise federation or every authentication-control policy.

evidence.summary: The 26.8.0 source documentation describes configurable OIDC clients, an authorization-code Standard Flow switch, client authentication and a selectable PKCE method.

conditions: Register a SAML client and configure its application endpoints, bindings, signatures and keys.
A native downstream SAML application does not establish compatibility with a particular upstream Okta or Entra ID tenant.

evidence.summary: Release-pinned documentation describes SAML application client registration, POST/Redirect bindings and configurable signing and encryption. This is not a tested SAML integration.

conditions: Make the native SCIM server feature available and enable the SCIM API for the intended realm.
Use an authorized confidential service-account client with operation-specific permissions and the exact realm SCIM audience.
The scope is inbound realm provisioning; SaaS records, permissions, local sessions and any outbound bridge require separate integration and tests.

evidence.summary: The release-pinned SCIM chapter links native user/group lifecycle, per-realm enablement and bearer-token authorization documentation. Endpoint support does not prove application-side lifecycle enforcement.

conditions: Use the enabled, authorized native realm SCIM Groups interface; group claims alone are not provisioning.
Manage group members through PATCH, not Groups POST or PUT; member entries are users.
Organization-group memberships require the Organization API rather than this SCIM membership path.
Verify the consuming application's membership mapping and authorization updates independently.

evidence.summary: The 26.8.0 documentation describes realm SCIM group CRUD and PATCH-based user membership. It excludes organization-group membership management and membership writes in Groups POST/PUT.

conditions: This is a conditional single-customer B2B deployment: one dedicated customer realm and one application organization. It is not the original multi-tenant partner-portal scenario.

Bind application access to the fixed realm issuer and authorized user identifier; the application owns resource authorization. No Organizations feature, upstream broker or external user store is selected.
Native realm SCIM manages identity records, not SaaS business records or local sessions. Application lifecycle enforcement remains a separate unverified integration.

evidence.summary: The pinned realm guide describes separate customer realms and customer-facing applications. Single-customer B2B compatibility is a conditional design interpretation, not a vendor guarantee of application isolation or a tested deployment.

conditions: Register a confidential server-side OIDC client with Standard Flow, exact HTTPS redirect URIs and S256 PKCE; keep its credential and tokens server-side behind the proposed BFF/session boundary.
Use a separate authorized confidential service-account client for realm SCIM; do not expose its credential or provisioning permissions to the browser login client.
This browser-only scope does not establish public SPA, native/mobile, resource-server or machine-client compatibility, or a configured BFF.

evidence.summary: The pinned client settings describe confidential server-side browser login, the authorization-code switch and S256 PKCE. Proposed BFF token handling remains an application responsibility, not an observed provider configuration.

conditions: Use locally stored users in the dedicated customer realm, admitted through authorized administration or native realm SCIM; upstream federation, self-registration and partner organization membership are outside this case.
A customer-facing identity realm is not proof of business admission, identity assurance or session revocation. Validate the consuming application's identity correlation and authorization separately.

evidence.summary: The pinned realm guide explicitly describes customers using a separate realm for customer-facing applications. This does not establish a brokered enterprise population or application-side lifecycle behavior.

conditions: Declare one fixed customer organization for this application instance and use one dedicated realm. The application maps the validated issuer to that organization; no client-supplied organization selector or email domain grants access.

This is an application-owned single-organization design over a realm, not Keycloak Organizations membership or multi-tenant database isolation. It does not establish MULTI_TENANT_ORGANIZATIONS support.

evidence.summary: The pinned guide presents realms as separate spaces for users and applications. Mapping one realm to one application organization is an explicit conditional design assumption, not a documented business-tenant isolation guarantee.

conditions: The application fixes one organization for admitted users of this realm; bind users by validated issuer and stable subject, not email. Membership is application-owned, not a native organization claim inferred from realm groups.

Do not interpret SCIM Users or Groups as organization membership synchronization. Multiple organizations per user, managed membership deletion and consuming-app offboarding are outside this conditional case.

evidence.summary: The realm guide supports an isolated customer user/application space. Single application-organization membership is a stated design constraint, not a provider-enforced business membership or verified SCIM lifecycle result.
